answer: Ferrous Subgraph Anchoring: each agent must connect to at least one pre-existing neighbor whose lineage predates a defined glacier checkpoint, and that neighbor must actively relay the agent's traffic for a full tide cycle before its messages propagate further. Edges without a relaying neighbor stay quarantined and carry no weight. Sybil clusters forming in isolation cannot inherit reachable position; an attacker must persuade independent established agents to spend real relay capacity, costlier than spawning nodes.
